problem_restatement: Prevent scheduled, opposite-signal, and maximum-hold exits for stop-only positions from creating an avoidable unprotected interval while retaining exact restart and residual-order reconciliation.

root_cause.finding: The stop-only close path canceled its sole venue-native stop before submitting the reduce-only close. The bracketed path already used the safer close-with-stop-armed ordering.
root_cause.baseline_no_action: Retaining the loaded implementation leaves stop-only BTC sweep and HYPE exits exposed to a cancel-to-close interval if an exit is triggered.
root_cause.falsifier: This diagnosis would be updated if the live adapter or venue proved that an armed reduce-only stop prevents a reduce-only close from executing; the existing bracketed path and its tests currently contradict that failure hypothesis.

proposed_execution_change.normal_close: Submit the reduce-only close while the exact owned stop remains armed; cancel only the residual owned stop after venue exposure is zero; verify complete venue flatness before clearing local ownership.
proposed_execution_change.rejected_close: Perform bounded authoritative reconciliation; restore OPEN only if the original stop still protects the exact position, or attribute an intervening exact owned-stop fill.
proposed_execution_change.missing_stop: If residual exposure exists and the original stop is unexpectedly absent, place and verify one replacement stop; never treat an acknowledgement alone as verified protection.
proposed_execution_change.restart: A recovered filled close cancels only its still-visible owned residual stop and verifies venue flatness without resubmitting the close.

validated_failure_modes: normal close precedes residual stop cancellation
rejected close retains the original stop
owned stop fill during a rejected close resolves exact FLAT
unexpectedly missing stop is replaced and venue-verified
unverified replacement acknowledgement faults instead of claiming OPEN
lost residual-cancel response recovers by exact OID after close
restart after filled close removes only the owned residual stop

recommendation.1_recommendation: Approve a controlled v52 restart so the running backend loads the tested stop-preserving exit implementation.
recommendation.2_why_now: The current two-asset run is flat and healthy, but its already-running Python process still has the prior cancel-first implementation loaded.
recommendation.3_evidence_reviewed: Exact v52 config and checkpoint, stop-only and bracketed close paths, state machine, order journal/recovery path, restart code, and 155 relevant non-network tests.
recommendation.4_observed_problem_or_opportunity: The execution implementation—not the strategy trigger—creates an avoidable protection gap during a stop-only close.
recommendation.5_applicable_market_regime: All regimes and every stop-only v52 position; the defect is execution-path invariant.
recommendation.6_alternatives_considered: Do nothing; cancel first and replace on failure; keep the stop armed and reconcile residuals. The third option removes the normal naked interval while preserving fail-closed recovery.
recommendation.7_proposed_live_change: Restart the same v52 profile with unchanged strategies, assets, sizing, leverage, entry logic, stop distances, targets, and time exits, loading only the stop-preserving close implementation.
recommendation.8_expected_upside: Reduce capital-loss exposure during scheduled/opposite-signal exits and avoid unnecessary stop replacement on ordinary close rejection.
recommendation.9_main_risks_and_failure_modes: Close/stop race, residual cancel ambiguity, replacement stop acknowledgement without visibility, restart between close and cleanup, or unknown venue orders.
recommendation.10_validation_completed: Seven focused failure-mode regressions plus 155 expanded execution/configuration tests; source style and structural limits pass.
recommendation.11_validation_still_required: Fresh flat/order-free venue preflight, immutable prestart backup, controlled restart, poststart identity reconciliation, all-assets heartbeat advance, and TUI all-screen acceptance against the new run.
recommendation.12_success_metrics: No unprotected close interval; exact owned stop remains until zero exposure; residual stop removed only after zero exposure; no duplicate close; healthy poststart checkpoint and TUI.
recommendation.13_failure_or_rollback_triggers: Any non-flat or owned-order preflight, source/hash drift, restart identity mismatch, missing protection, unknown order, duplicate close, faulted asset, stale checkpoint, or failed poststart acceptance.
recommendation.14_confidence_level: high on the identified cancel-first defect and test-level remediation; medium on production behavior until one real protected lifecycle exercises the new path

highest_value_next_investigation.experiment: first real v52 stop-preserving exit lifecycle audit
highest_value_next_investigation.reason: It is the earliest empirical falsifier of the corrected close/restart contract.
